text:
olivia (capacity-planning): quick heads-up — our Q3 reserved GPU model (hosted-api demand + CanaryX) shows a potential ~18% underutilization in eu-west committed pool unless we adjust mix or run additional workloads. looking for quick ideas/assumptions to sweep
maya (eng-infra): do you have the demand curve and the booking horizon? can we backtest on last q's traffic?
sam (finance): FYI finance saw a weird early-termination charge on the last reserved contract renewal — might affect net cost calc. i'll pull the bill detail. :eyes:
nora (eng-sre): underutilization worries are real but we also saw tail latency spikes when we tried auto-burst across regions last month. need to ensure cross-region routing doesn't violate data-locality for enterprise tenants.
jeff (eng-infra): agree. we could run a sensitivity sweep: vary hosted traffic + feature lift (+10/+25/+50%) against committed supply, plus scenarios: (1) keep current commitments, (2) shift 20% to short-term spot pools with auto-fallback, (3) enable pooled burst across eu & na for non-PII workloads.
liam (product-ops): CanaryX true uplift is uncertain — marketing plans a big push in week 4 of Q3, but conversion could be much lower. include a pessimistic scenario where uplift = 0.
olivia (capacity-planning): thanks. i'll run the sweep but need two things: (A) last 12 weeks of per-region avg token/sec and p95 latency buckets, (B) exact committed GPU counts and SKU mix (a100v2 vs a10g) per contract.
maya (eng-infra): attaching quick snippet of how we bucketed last time: ```
# demand aggregation
for job in hosted_requests:
  region = job.region
  epoch_bucket = floor(job.ts / 300)
  agg[region][epoch_bucket].tokens += job.tokens
```
jeff (eng-infra): also call out billing shapes: some committed contracts have flat refunds on early termination, others prorated credits. sam can we centralize that mapping?
sam (finance): yes i'll map contract_id -> termination_policy and share. also i want the model to report expected committed-utilization and expected incremental cost per 1% drop in utilization.
nora (eng-sre): operational note — if we decide pooled burst, we'll need routing guards: tenant tags, strict region allowlist, and a fallback to local small instances for regulated tenants. that adds ~2-4% overhead to utilization (safety margin).
liam (product-ops): timeline: product needs a recommendation for exec by EOD Friday. can we get an initial sensitivity table by Thursday?
olivia (capacity-planning): yes i can produce first pass by Thu EOD. action items: olivia run sweep + base/pessimistic/optimistic scenarios; sam produce contract termination map + billing anomalies; maya/jeff provide last-12w per-region aggregates and current committed SKU counts; nora list routing constraints for pooled burst. i'll add the spreadsheet link when ready.
maya (eng-infra): noted. i'll also flag any infra changes that need runbook updates.
sam (finance): pulling bill now — will post cost delta numbers in this thread when available. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
deploy-bot: deployment complete: capacity-collector v2 -> staging (sha:abc123)
olivia (capacity-planning): perfect, thanks all. if anyone has customer-specific commitments that would block pooled usage, ping me directly. :pray:
jeff (eng-infra): one suggestion — consider a small buffer of convertible reserved to burstable (e.g., 10% of commit) to hedge forecast error. low operational overhead and reduces cost risk.
liam (product-ops): agree — that's an easy exec-friendly recommendation (hedge with convertibles).
olivia (capacity-planning): adding that to the recommendation list. will share spreadsheet + expected cost delta scenarios (CSV) Thursday.
